Extroverted

EK-struh-vert-ed · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Extroverted is focused outwardly rather than inwardly; outgoing.

Being naturally extroverted, Diego found the isolation of remote work far harder than his quieter coworkers did.

Worked Example

At the reunion, the extroverted twin worked the entire room within twenty minutes, while her quieter brother stayed by the snack table the whole night.

Being energized by people and naturally drawn to talk to as many of them as possible is exactly what extroverted describes.

How Extroverted Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

outgoing

outgoing: sociable and comfortable meeting new people

gregarious

gregarious: fond of company; very sociable

Antonyms

introverted

introverted: focused inward, drained by too much socializing

reserved

reserved: slow to open up socially

How Strong Is It? — sociable → extroverted → gregarious

sociable vs. extroverted

sociable vs. extroverted: She was sociable enough to chat comfortably with a few new coworkers at lunch.

gregarious vs. extroverted

gregarious vs. extroverted: Gregarious is stronger than extroverted: an extroverted guest happily chats with the people nearby, while a gregarious one works the whole wedding, introducing himself to every single table.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — extro-

Prefix — extro-: outward, beyond (Latin, a variant of extra-)

Root — vert

Root — vert: to turn (from Latin vertere, 'to turn')

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: adjective-forming ending, 'made or marked by' (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Extroverted comes from extro- ('outward,' a variant of Latin extra-) + vert ('to turn,' from Latin vertere) + -ed -- literally 'turned outward.' An extroverted person's energy and attention turn outward, toward other people and the world, rather than inward.

Use the root in a new word: divert

Use the root in a new word: divert: Construction crews had to divert traffic onto a side street for the rest of the week.
